text.en: By resolution of the Ursus Central Executive Committee, Olga Danilovna Tripolieva, following her amnesty, joined the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and later, upon the recommendation of members of the Ursus Student Self-government Group, came to Rhodes Island to represent St. Petersburg in liaison and communication duties with Rhodes Island.
text.zh: 经乌萨斯中央执行委员会决议，奥尔佳·达尼洛夫娜·特里波列娃在受到豁免之后，进入外交部任职，后经由乌萨斯学生自治团成员们推荐，来到罗德岛，代表圣骏堡方面开展与罗德岛的联络沟通工作。

text.en:
Imaging tests show clear organ outlines and no abnormal shadows in the subject's thoracic cavity, with no abnormal particulate counts in the circulatory system, showing no signs of Oripathy infection. The subject is confirmed at this stage as uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 0%
Operator Olga shows no signs of being infected by Originium.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.11 u/L
Coming from a wealthy noble family, Olga has rarely been in contact with Originium, hence this indicator is relatively low. After we completed the various index tests on Olga, she politely asked if she might view the clinical diagnostic reports of other Ursus Infected.
Olga sat in the Medical Department's chair for a long time, reading report after report. Among them were plenty of Ursus miners, farmers, and those forced to live in the wilds, exposed to Catastrophes. She stared at the numbers on the reports as if trying to commit every single one to memory. When she finally stood up, she bowed to us—a formal courtesy, but she looked more like she was expressing her gratitude.
We gave Olga a tour of the Medical Department, and afterward, she wrote a letter to Ivan Turchin. It is said the letter contained her vision for improving the living environment of the Ursus Infected, as well as her hopes of establishing closer cooperation with Rhodes Island in the days to come.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员奥尔佳没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.11u/L
出身于优渥的贵族家庭，奥尔佳甚少接触源石，因此该项指标数值较低。在我们完成对奥尔佳的各项指标检测后，她礼貌地询问是否能让她看一下其他乌萨斯感染者的临床诊断报告。
奥尔佳坐在医疗部的椅子上看了很久，一份接着一份。那里面不乏乌萨斯的矿工、农民，以及那些不得不生活在野外，暴露在天灾中的人。她盯着报告上的数字，仿佛要把它们全都记在心中。等到再站起来时，她向我们欠身——这是一种礼节，但她看起来更像是在致谢。
我们带奥尔佳参观了医疗部，事后，她向伊凡·图林写了封信。据说信中包含了她对于改善乌萨斯感染者所处环境的设想，以及未来的日子里，她希望能与罗德岛建立更紧密的合作。

text.en:
Upon arriving at Rhodes Island, Olga first paid visits to Amiya, Kaltsit, and Closure, then toured Rhodes Island's various departments. In the span of a week, she roughly clarified the functions and operational status of each department at Rhodes Island, and brilliantly executed the synchronization of information between St. Petersburg and Rhodes Island.
One day, as Olga was organizing her experiences at Rhodes Island in her notebook, she was suddenly tapped on the shoulder by a Liberi operator.
"Hello?" Olga looked up; she recognized the person—an operator working in the cafe. Whenever she arranged meetings with Rhodes Island operators, she would choose this cafe. It was also her favorite workspace. Over time, she had grown familiar with this individual. The Liberi operator smiled sheepishly and pulled out a small pouch, handing it over to Olga. The pouch contained a substantial amount of chervonets, leaving Olga slightly startled.
"I didn't realize it at the time, and assumed the Rhodes Island cafe was just like the restaurants in St. Petersburg," Olga smiled, pulling out her Rhodes Island dining card from her waist. "You say I gave too much? It doesn't matter—after all, I occupied a table in the cafe for a long time. But that operator insisted on returning every last chervonets to me."
"On top of the price for what I ordered, I ought to give her an extra 'reward.' So I asked her, was there anything she wanted, or anything I could do for her?" Olga shifted her posture; her expression while recounting this remained confident and poised—much like she was conducting official business. "You ask what the 'reward' was?" She smiled. "That... is a secret. Forgive me for not sharing."

After spending another week at Rhodes Island, Olga gradually began to integrate into the environment and adapt to the atmosphere here. For instance—she learned she could apply to place a coffee maker on her dormitory desk so she could enjoy fine coffee while working in her room; meetings could be scheduled via the terminal without needing to write a letter two days in advance to confirm. (Closure had quite a few feelings about this, admitting that she sometimes truly couldn't make head or tail of the... somewhat "flamboyant" Ursus greeting phrasing in Olga's letters.)
"She even suffered 'merciless mockery' from Zofia over this. But as you know, the two of them... well, it was just a joke after all. Olga confiscated Zofia's honey drops as 'retribution' for the 'teasing,'" Rosa said, "though she didn't take all of them, leaving Zofia with a daily allowance of one."
"As for the people of Rhodes Island, and Rhodes Island itself... I still have a lot to learn," Olga said, her tone carrying a hint of lingering sentiment. "In two weeks, I feel I've only... scratched the surface."
"Of course," Zofia said. "You don't even know which coffee in the cafe is the best yet. Hehe, how about we go together later?"

The Personnel Department asked the Liberi operator from the cafe what the "reward" Olga mentioned actually was. The Liberi operator blushed furiously and finally stammered out—the ears peeking out from under Olga's hat looked fluffy, and she just wanted to pet Olga's ears.
text.zh:
来到罗德岛后，奥尔佳首先去拜访了阿米娅、凯尔希与可露希尔，随后参观了罗德岛的各个部门。她用一周时间大概厘清了罗德岛各个部门的职能与工作状态，并出色地完成了圣骏堡与罗德岛之间的信息同步工作。
某天，奥尔佳在笔记本上整理她在罗德岛的见闻时，突然被一位黎博利干员拍了拍肩膀。
“您好？”奥尔佳抬起头，她认得对方，是在咖啡厅工作的干员。每次约罗德岛的干员进行洽谈，她都会选在这个咖啡厅。这也是她最喜欢的办公场地。久而久之，她已经认识了这个人。黎博利干员不好意思地笑了笑，拿出一个小袋子，递给她。这袋子中装着不少切尔文，让奥尔佳微微有些惊愕。
“当时我并不知道这一点，还以为罗德岛的咖啡厅和圣骏堡的餐厅一样。”奥尔佳笑了笑，从腰间摸出罗德岛的饭卡，“你说我给多了？不重要——我毕竟占用了咖啡厅的桌子很久。但那位干员却执意要将所有切尔文都还给我。”
“在应付的价格之外，我应当给她额外的‘报酬’。因此我问她，有什么想要的，或是我能够为她做的？”奥尔佳换了个姿势，她讲述这件事时神情依然自信、坦然——甚至就像洽谈公务时一样。“你问‘报酬’是什么？”她笑了，“这一点……保密。恕我不能相告。”

在罗德岛又度过了一周之后，奥尔佳才开始逐渐融入这里的环境，适应这里的氛围。例如——她知道了可以申请在宿舍的办公桌上放一个咖啡机，这样在宿舍办公时她也能喝到上好的咖啡；而预约会议可以在终端上完成，不必提前两天写信确认。（可露希尔对此颇有感触，她承认，自己有时确实看不懂奥尔佳信中那些……稍有些“华丽”的乌萨斯问候辞藻。）
“她甚至因为这件事遭到了烈夏的‘无情嘲笑’。不过你也知道，她们两个……那毕竟只是玩笑而已。奥尔佳收走了烈夏的蜂蜜糖，作为对‘嘲笑’的‘回敬’。”凛冬说，“但没有全部拿走，给烈夏留了一天一颗的量。”
“对于罗德岛的人，以及罗德岛本身……我还有许多要学习的事。”说这话的时候，奥尔佳甚至略带些感叹，“两周的时间，我觉得自己还是……只触碰到了皮毛。”
“那当然。”烈夏说，“你还不知道咖啡厅最好喝的咖啡是哪款呢。哼哼，等会一起去怎么样？”

人事部询问了那位咖啡厅的黎博利干员，奥尔佳口中的“报酬”到底是什么。黎博利干员憋红了脸，最终支支吾吾地说——奥尔佳从帽子里露出来的耳朵看起来毛茸茸的，她想摸摸奥尔佳的耳朵。

text.en:
After meeting with members of the Ursus Student Self-government Group, Istina took Olga to get a Rhodes Island library card and recommended a novel to her. The novel told the story of a group of young people who bravely rebelled against injustice and oppression, ultimately achieving success. Olga finished reading the book in a single afternoon. By evening, she knocked on Istina's dorm door, carrying the book with her.

"Didn't you notice anything wrong?" Anna asked me while buttoning her shirt. "This is a story about the ultimate victory of idealism... but can victory be achieved simply through slogans and a negotiation or two with the nobles?"
"My intuition tells me no." Anna pulled my hand to the search terminal in the Rhodes Island library and typed in the book's title. The search results glaringly displayed two versions—one of which was not collected by Rhodes Island due to a publication ban. Anna looked at me. "This book is famous... extremely famous. Haven't you read it?"
I was momentarily speechless. Of course I had read this book... but it wasn't the same version Anna had read. In the version that didn't pass imperial censorship, the naive young people ultimately failed—their romance shattered, their ideals broken. The pair of young lovers Anna loved so dearly didn't stay together either; one died and the other was wounded. After hesitating for a moment, I still told Anna how the story originally went.
As I told her, I didn't quite dare look Anna in the eyes.
She fell silent. I secretly glanced sideways at her; Anna seemed... indeed a bit sad. To keep her from feeling sad, I spoke up: "They must have had some other way to survive, to keep living." At that, determined to go all the way, I turned on the lights in the Rhodes Island library, pulled her to sit at the table, and hauled out several weighty tomes fitting that era. History, law, novels... surely in one of them we would find a possibility, a way for those young people to live on, for the characters she loved to stay together through all the springs that were bound to come... In the end, we got our wish.
This story indeed had other versions, but reality offered no second path. The things I had done suddenly struck me like a bolt of lightning, leaving me trembling uncontrollably. I remembered Anna holding my hand, I remembered Antoshka's list... What a horrifying consequence I had brought about! So many vibrant lives, every single one of them young people just like me, perished because of my arrogance and naivety—
...Perhaps these words had been pent up inside me for too long, reminding me that I still had an apology left unsaid. So I took Anna by both hands and apologized to her. For the Student Union, for everything that happened in the theater, for my childishness, naivety, and self-righteousness. She shook her head and brought up how I had previously pushed against all opposition to invite the Student Self-government Group to join the Student Union. She wanted to comfort me, I knew... That event truly happened, yet it could not erase my fault. I finished speaking and waited for Anna to reply.
Anna said she had never blamed me. She pushed the books, paper, and pens beside her toward me: "We've already succeeded." She stared at the badge on my chest representing the New Ursus, smiling once more.
—Narrated by Operator Olga, authorized by the operator herself
text.zh:
与乌萨斯学生自治团的成员们见面后，真理带奥尔佳去办了罗德岛的图书借阅证，并向她推荐了一本小说。这本小说讲述了一群年轻人勇敢反抗不公与压迫，最终成功的故事。奥尔佳很快读完了这本书，仅用了一个下午。傍晚，她敲开真理的宿舍门，带着这本书。

“你没有发现什么不对劲的地方吗？”安娜边扣着衬衫纽扣，边向我发问，“这讲述的是理想主义最终胜利的故事……但，胜利仅仅是靠口号、靠一两场和贵族之间的斡旋就能达成的吗？”
“直觉告诉我不是这样。”安娜拉着我的手，到罗德岛图书室的查询终端上输入这本书的名字。搜索结果赫然呈现两个版本——其中一个版本因禁止发行而并未被罗德岛收录。安娜看向我，“这本书很有名……非常有名。你难道没看过吗？”
我语塞了一会。我当然看过这本书……但和安娜看的并不是同一个版本。未通过帝国审查的版本中，天真的年轻人们最终失败——爱情破碎，理想破裂。安娜所喜欢的、那一对相爱的年轻人也并未携手相伴，而是一死一伤。犹豫了一会，我还是告诉了安娜这个故事最初的样子。
告诉她的时候，我有点不敢看安娜的眼睛。
她沉默。我悄悄偏过头看她，安娜似乎……确实有些难过。为了不让她难过，我开口：“他们一定还有什么别的办法，能够活下来，活下去。”说到这，我决定一不做二不休，于是打开罗德岛图书室的灯，拉她坐到桌前，搬出几本符合那个时代的大部头。历史、法律、小说……总有一种可能，我们会找到一种可能，那群年轻人会活下去，她所喜爱的角色会相伴一生，走过必定会到来的一个又一个春天……最后，我们如愿以偿。
这个故事的确有其他的版本，但现实却没有第二条路可选。我曾做过的那些事突然像闪电一般击中了我，令我战栗不止。我想起安娜曾拉住我的手，想起安托沙的那份名单……我曾造成多么可怖的后果啊！曾有那么多鲜活的生命，他们无一不是与我一样的年轻人，却因我的傲慢与天真而丧命——
……也许是这些话积压在我心里太久，它们提醒着我，我还有一个道歉没有完成。所以我拉住安娜的双手，向她道歉。为了学生联合大会，为了剧院中发生的一切，为了我的幼稚、天真，和自以为是。她摇摇头，说起之前我力排众议请学生自治团加入学生联合大会的事。她想安慰我，我知道……那件事确实发生了，却无法抵消我的过错。我讲完了，等待着安娜开口。
安娜说，她从未怪过我。她将一旁的书籍和纸笔推到我面前：“我们已经成功了。”她盯着我胸前那枚代表着新乌萨斯的徽章，再次微笑起来，“来吧，让我们再成功一次。”
——来自干员奥尔佳的讲述，人事部已得到干员本人的授权

text.en:
[Excerpt from a News Commentary]
...Grand Duchess Yelizaveta has arrived in St. Petersburg and declared her intention to support Grand Princess Anastasia... to reverse the chaotic situation filling the city with panic... It is reported that the Second and Fourth Armies remain stationed around St. Petersburg... What exactly are the Grand Duchess's motives? Earlier, the St. Petersburg Gazette published... The emperor is missing, whereabouts unknown... Will Prime Minister Islam Vit step forward?... Or... The parliament has yet to announce...

[Excerpt from a Tabloid]
As Vit withdraws outside the city, the grand nobles within the city face a situation where they must make a choice... Withdraw from St. Petersburg, or defect to the Grand Duchess... It is rumored that Duke Danila Tripoliev may already be planning his next move... Return to ancestral lands?... Leave St. Petersburg?...

[A Record, Reconstructed from Various Accounts]
"Olga... Chairperson, no, Your Excellency, we've found... this." A student handed a clipping into Olga's hands.
"...Many grand nobles within the city have already defected to the Grand Duchess! Headed by Tripoliev's daughter... Still a student status... Rumors claim Tripoliev's daughter had a falling out with her father, perhaps related to the events that occurred in the Katoga District... Break?...
Progressive youth?...
Betraying one's forebears?...
Fair-weather friend?..."
Olga read the words on the clipping. Nothing more than more speculation about her capitulation to the Grand Duchess. To acknowledge Olga's "loyalty," the title following her name had been changed to "Duke." After her father withdrew outside the city, that empty estate fell entirely under Olga's administration.
Opinions varied; some newspapers pilloried her, calling her a fair-weather friend who betrayed her forebears, while others adopted a wait-and-see attitude, yet dug up every piece of information they could get their hands on, attempting to pigeonhole Olga with ambiguous phrasing.
"...A negative example." Olga flicked the piece of paper in her hand. "Our newspaper must discard old, ambiguous, cowardly phrasing." She scrutinized the clipping. "The layout style, however, is worth studying."
A student nearby stammered a bit. "It's not... It's you. This is too... They're saying such awful things! And some other students, after you... became a Duke, they also..."
Olga pasted the clipping into her notebook with glue. "The clipping itself doesn't matter, but this information should be collected; I'll preserve it." She stood up, straightened her collar, and walked out the door, where many students had gathered, waiting for Olga's answer.
"I am no longer Chairperson, nor am I 'Your Excellency.' Just call me Olga, like we did back at school."

[A Handwritten Note in a Notebook, with a Clipping Pasted on the Back]
Is doing this right? The newspaper office's work isn't going smoothly. Manpower, equipment, censorship... We lack sufficient support in every aspect. Even idle gossip has begun to circulate that Tripoliev's child is going to inherit a title and swear allegiance... I know that Grand Duchess is watching me. Waiting for me—Tripoliev's daughter. Should it be me...? Can I really...?
...Is there anyone who can give me an answer? Father? Teacher? Comrades?
(A very long blank space)
Only yourself.
Keep going, Olga Danilovna Tripolieva.
text.zh:
【某段新闻评论节选】
……叶莉萨维塔女大公已来到圣骏堡城内，并宣称将扶持纳斯塔霞皇女……扭转城内人心惶惶的混乱局面……据称，第二、第四集团军仍在圣骏堡周边驻扎……女大公究竟有何企图？先前《圣骏堡公报》已刊载……皇帝失踪，下落不明……伊斯拉姆·维特总理将出面？……抑或……议会仍未对外宣布……

【某段小报节选】
随着维特撤出城外，城内大贵族已面临着不得不做出选择的局面……撤出圣骏堡，抑或投靠女大公……据称，达尼拉·特里波列夫公爵或许已有行动的打算……回到祖地？……离开圣骏堡？……

【某段记录，根据不同人的转述还原而成】
“奥尔佳……主席，不，阁下，我们发现了……这个。”一个学生将剪报递到奥尔佳的手中。
“……已有不少城内大贵族投靠女大公！以特里波列夫家的女儿为首……还是学生身份……传言称特里波列夫家的女儿曾与父亲有过罅隙，也许是和卡托加区发生的事件有关……决裂？……进步青年？……背叛父辈？……墙头草？……”
奥尔佳阅读着剪报上的文字。无非又是些对她向女大公投诚的猜测。为表彰奥尔佳的“忠心”，她名字后的称谓变为了“公爵”，父亲撤出城外后，那座空荡荡的庄园，也全权归在奥尔佳的管理之下。
众说纷纭，有报纸对她口诛笔伐，称她为背叛父辈的墙头草；有报纸持观望态度，却极尽所能地挖掘一切能挖到的信息，试图用暧昧不清的话语为奥尔佳定性。
“……反面案例。”奥尔佳扬了扬手中的纸张，“我们的报纸要摒弃旧有的、暧昧的、懦弱的语句。”她仔细端详了一下剪报，“排版方式倒是可供学习。”
一旁的学生有些吞吞吐吐。“不是的……是你。这对你……他们说得太过分了！还有一些同学，在你……成了公爵之后，也……”
奥尔佳将剪报用胶水粘贴在自己的笔记本上。“剪报本身并不重要，但这些信息应该被收集，我会将它留存。”她站起身，正了正衣领，走向门外，不少学生聚集于此，等待着奥尔佳的回答。
“我不再是主席，也不会是‘阁下’。还是像在学校里那样，叫我奥尔佳吧。”

【某段本子上的手写记录，背面贴着一份剪报】
这样做是对的吗？报社的工作进行得并不顺利。人手、器材、审查……我们缺乏足够的支持，各方面都是。甚至已有闲言碎语开始流传，特里波列夫家的孩子要继承爵位，宣誓效忠……我知道，那位女大公在看着我。等待着我——特里波列夫的女儿。该由我……？我真的能……
……有谁能给我答案？父亲？老师？同伴？
（一段很长的空白）
只有你自己。
坚持下去，奥尔佳·达尼洛夫娜·特里波列娃。

text.en:
"The reason I feel anger is because I refuse to live in a lie... to survive a life built on deception. To live, and to not tell lies—that is the simplest thing we can do!"
Recalling the past of the Petrashevsky circle, Olga recited this classic theatrical monologue word for word. She confessed to us that upon learning everything, her thoughts were in such disarray that she felt almost numb. During that time, her mind kept returning to this monologue.
The Medical Department conducted a prudent evaluation of this and consulted several Operators who frequently interacted with Olga. None of them knew of any conversation between Olga and Antosha; whatever transpired is perhaps a story only Olga herself can tell.
"Before Olga found Antosha, I had a chat with her... She was very calm, as if she were prepared to accept the truth. That truth must have dealt her quite a blow; she was merely silent, but not despondent. After just a short while, she had already pulled herself together... At least, so it seemed. Her movements were even quicker than before. Clearly, she spoke more, thought more, and did more."
—Operator Truth

[An Interview Record]
There is nothing off-limits. If this helps Rhodes Island understand me better... After all, a good negotiation is built upon trust. All of this is in the past for me, and looking to the future is what everyone ought to do... No need for an official tone here? Very well, I will adjust. My words just now merely demonstrated my candor.
...What was I thinking? My true thoughts... Guilt. Questioning my own naivety, wondering why I hadn't noticed sooner. Anxiety. Desiring to know the condition of my comrades all the sooner, to see if there was anything within my power that I could do.
Teacher... Yes, I always think of him. Antosha told me about the days when he and Matvey went to school. Back then, Teacher only taught the history of literature; it wasn't until my generation that the writing composition class was added.
(A period of silence)
Whenever I read history, I always wonder: in the past, there were so many emperors with monumental achievements, so many privileged nobles, so many people who wanted to rebel. Why is the life I possess something others cannot have? I know I cannot arbitrarily bestow noble titles upon anyone, but... why am I not even worthy of possessing the ability to save my teacher and comrades?
To live... and to not tell lies. If I acknowledge the lie, then I, too, become a liar.
Yes, a single monologue from a play, known by very few. It comes from a play they refused to let me perform on the days when everyone was forced to repeat lies.
This is not right. The logic is just that simple. That is all I wanted to say.
To put it into practice.

[Comments on a Composition]
After reading Olga's composition, many students always give a "standard" evaluation. Admittedly, one can perceive good upbringing in her writing, but it goes beyond that. Many authors are skilled in flowery diction and exaggeration, yet the heart behind their writing is empty and cold. An empty heart can be used to fill different things—filled with lies, inexplicable allegiance, or betrayal. But Olga's writing... though it shares that beautiful diction, behind it lies a full, burning heart. She still has a long road of life ahead of her. Pessimistically speaking, perhaps one day the flame will grow cold... but it will never vanish. Once ignited, it has no room for anything else.
—Petrashevsky, evaluated on Month X, Day X
text.zh:
“我之所以感到愤怒，是因为我不想生活在谎言中……在被欺骗的生活中生存。活着，而且不撒谎，这是我们能做到的最简单的事情！”
在讲述彼得拉设夫斯基小组的往事时，奥尔佳原封不动地背诵了这一段经典的戏剧独白。她向我们坦陈，得知了一切之后，她思绪太过繁杂，甚至有些浑浑噩噩。那段时间，她总是想到这段独白。
医疗部对此进行了审慎的评估，并询问了与奥尔佳往来频繁的几位干员。她们对奥尔佳与安托沙的交谈均不知情，发生了什么，也许只有奥尔佳本人可以讲述。
“在奥尔佳找到安托沙之前，我和她聊了一次……她很冷静，就像已经预备好接受真相一样。那真相一定对她造成了不小的冲击，她只是沉默，但没有消沉。仅仅是一小段时间过后，她便已经振作了……至少看起来是这样。她的动作甚至比之前更快。很明显，她说得更多，想得更多，做得也更多。”
——干员真理

【一段访谈记录】
没什么不可以问的。如果这能让罗德岛更深地了解我……毕竟，好的洽谈建立在信任之上。这一切对我而言都已经过去，而看向未来更是所有人理应要做的事……在这里不需要公事公办的语气？好的，我会调整。刚才的话只是表明我的坦诚。
……我想了什么？真实的想法……愧疚。质问自己的天真，为何没有早一些发现。焦急。想再快一点得知同伴们的状况，看看有什么我力所能及的事。
老师……是的，我总会想到他。安托沙和我讲述了他与马特维上学时的事，那时老师只教授文学史这一门课程，到我这一届，才增设了习文写作课。
（一段沉默）
阅读历史的时候我总在想，过去有那么多居功至伟的帝王，那么多优渥的贵族，那么多想要反抗的人。为什么，我所拥有的生活其他人不能拥有？我知道自己不能让谁莫名其妙地就冠上贵族的头衔，但……为什么我连拯救老师与同伴的能力都不配拥有？
活着……而且不撒谎。如果我承认谎言，那我就也成了撒谎的人。
是的，剧中的一句独白，很少有人知道它。它来自一部，在所有人都要重复谎言的日子里，他们不让我出演的戏剧。
这样不对。道理就这一个。我想说的就是这些。
为了践行它。

【一段习作评语】
许多同学在阅读奥尔佳的习作后，总会给出“标准”的评价。诚然，你能从她的习作中看出良好的教养，但不仅于此。许多作者善用靡丽的文辞和夸饰，文章背后的心却是空的、冷的。空荡的心可以用来填充不同的事物——填充谎言、不明所以的效忠或背叛。但奥尔佳的文章……同样有美丽的辞藻，背后却是已经被填满的、火热的心。她还有漫长的人生道路要走。悲观地讲，也许某天火焰会冷下来……但不会消失。一旦被点燃过，就再容不下其他的事物。
——彼得拉设夫斯基，评于X月X日

text.en:
[An Inaugural Address]
"First, please allow me to introduce myself. My name is Olga Danilovna Tripolyova. On the 13th of this month, Ivan Tulin appointed me to the newly established Ministry of Foreign Affairs as a diplomat. Who could have imagined... in my childhood, my vague vision for the future was to become a playwright.
Perhaps there is a shared essence. It is likewise the employment of words and eloquence, and the content spoken and discussed concerns the lives of the people in this ancient country.
Here is your beautiful homeland. The waters of Lake Neva flow ever onward, Ursus possesses a heavy, biting snow, hollies that do not fade even in the harsh winter, and outside the window—colleagues, it also possesses the brand-new sunlight of spring.
So that everyone may stop to admire it, so that everyone may freely express their feelings—to write poetry, to compose music, to wish to become a playwright and indeed become one... I fear we have a long way to go on this path.
Fortunately, this place has never lacked those who dare to forge ahead. To be able to stand here, to become a part of it... I am deeply honored."
text.zh:
【一段上任致辞】
“首先，请允许我自我介绍一下。我叫奥尔佳·达尼洛夫娜·特里波列娃。本月13日，伊凡·图林任命我进入新成立的外交部工作，任外交官一职。谁能想到……在我幼时，对未来模糊不清的设想，竟然是成为一名剧作家。
也许有异曲同工之妙。同样是运用文字与口才，所讲述和讨论的内容也是关于这个古老国家中人们的生活。
这里是各位美丽的家乡。涅瓦湖水始终流淌，乌萨斯拥有厚重凛冽的雪，拥有在严冬也不褪色的冬青，而窗外——同僚们，她也拥有全新的，春日的阳光。
为了让人人都可以驻足欣赏，人人都可以自由地抒发感情——写诗，作曲，想成为一名剧作家，就成为一名剧作家……恐怕我们要在这条道路上前进很久。
但好在，这里从不缺乏勇于前进的人。能站在这里，成为其中的一员……我深感荣幸。”
